AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring charter
buses to use commercial global positioning system technology
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2978

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring
charter buses to use commercial global positioning system technology

 
PURPOSE:

To ensure that every charter bus has a commercial global positioning
system while operating in New York.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the vehicle and traffic law by adding section 509-dd,
which requires that every charter bus must have a commercial global
positioning system in order to operate in New York. For this purpose, a
charter bus will be any bus transporting passengers for compensation in
chartered party, where the two groups have a common purpose and under a
single contract agree to a specific destination and itinerary. The
commercial global positioning system is any system that is specifically
designed to assist navigation of commercial vehicles, which included
finding routes with minimum clearance of the bus.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

There have been incidents in which charter buses have hit the overpass
injuring many of the passengers on board due to the use of an everyday
global positioning application rather than one made for commercial use.
These everyday applications were created for cars and will suggest park-
ways as potential routes even though parkways are not made for commer-
cial traffic. Commercial global positioning systems were created for
commercial vehicles and will not suggest a route that a commercial vehi-
cle could not take. The commercial systems take into consideration the
height of the bus, and will suggest only routes in which the overpasses
meet the minimum requirement for the bus. This would ensure that all
commercial buses would only drive on roads that are safe for a vehicle
of that size.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.8207 of 2018

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE PATE:

Immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2978A

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requiring
charter buses to use commercial global positioning system technology

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To ensure that charter buses have a commercial global positioning
system.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the Vehicle and Traffic Law by adding a new subdivision
52 to section 375 to require every charter bus registered in the State
be equipped with commercial global positioning system technology, and to
prohibit any person from operating, or causing the operation, of a char-
ter bus registered in the State unless it is equipped with the required
commercial GPS technology.

Section 2 provides that the act would be deemed repealed if any federal
agency or any court of competent jurisdiction finally determines that
the act would render New York State out of compliance with federal law
or regulation.

Section 3 provides a severability clause. Section 4 is the effective
date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

There have been incidents in which charter busses have hit the overpass
injuring many of the passengers on board due to the use of an everyday
global positioning application rather than one made for commercial use.
These everyday applications were created for cars and will suggest park-
ways as potential routes even though parkways are not made for commer-
cial traffic. Commercial global positioning systems were created for
commercial vehicles and will not suggest a route that a commercial vehi-
cle could not take. The commercial systems take into account the height
of the bus, and will suggest only routes in which the overpasses meet
the minimum height requirement for the bus. This would ensure that all
commercial busses would only drive on roads that are safe for a vehicle
of that size.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.8207 of 2018.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law;
provided that the commissioner of transportation shall notify the legis-
lative bill drafting commission upon the occurrence of the provisions of
section two of this act in order that the commission may maintain an
accurate and timely effective data base of the official text of the laws
of the state of New York in furtherance of effectuating the provisions
of section 44 of the legislative law and section 70-b of the public
officers law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment and/or
repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of
this act on its effective date are authorized to be made and completed
on or before such effective date.

summary: Requires charter buses to use commercial global positioning system technology which takes into account the minimum clearance of the motor vehicle.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 177
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 2978-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to requir-
      ing  charter  buses  to  use  commercial global positioning system
      technology"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would require every charter bus registered in New York State
to be equipped with commercial global positioning (GPS)  technology.  It
would  be  unlawful  to  operate  a charter bus on any public highway or
private road absent such technology.
 
  While the intent of this legislation is laudable, it presents a number
of difficulties which ultimately makes it  impracticable.  There  is  no
national  standard for commercial GPS technology. The lack of a national
standard may yield inconsistent or inaccurate results in the performance
of any particular commercial GPS brand. Determining the adequacy of  any
particular  device  would lead to challenges with enforcing the require-
ment. Moreover, this legislation would only apply to charter buses  that
are  registered in New York State, and would not apply to commercial bus
services registered in other states. This could lead to confusion on the
part of the traveling public, who may expect all charter buses operating
in the State be equipped with commercial GPS.  For these reasons,  I  am
constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
